note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 by an independent auditor who authored none of the change, after 9b7673180c and 5a65ff5ee7 (spec-add-path-limit-send-receive). RFC 7911 Section 2: "However, the Path Identifier MUST be assigned in such a way that the BGP speaker is able to use the (Prefix, Path Identifier) to uniquely identify a path advertised to a neighbor." Two cited producers moved. session_write.go writeUpdateBody now calls s.pathsLimit.filter (the extracted PATHS-LIMIT admission, formerly s.filterPathsLimit) and, after commit, adjOutWrite.owePathsLimitElections, which owes an election per contested prefix into the destination's owed table: neither mints, rebinds or releases a Path Identifier. session_ownership.go adjOutWrite.allow's adjOutRecovery withdraw branch now lets an item marked pathsLimitDemotion withdraw an ADD-PATH key whose owner is current; it still returns before any identifier bookkeeping, still honours recoverySpares, and withdraws the (Prefix, Path Identifier) the destination already holds, so the recipient never sees two paths under one identifier. The identifier producers (forward_path_id.go) and both tagged units are byte-identical, each with its verified revert record on generatePath. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgements are in this file's git history. The same closure added a doc-comment paragraph to session_ownership.go beginAdjOut stating that the table mutex stays held until release and MUST NOT be taken again inside that window; the function body is unchanged.
